rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT CRIMINALIZING VIDEO AND PHOTO VOYEURISM AND IMPOSING PENALTIES THEREOF
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Voyeurism Act of 2003\".  With the advent of the internet and information technology, pictures are being downloaded, exchanged and passed on through the e-mail.  While some pictures are copyrighted, a number are stolen shots of people or groups caught in compromising situations.  This is a gross invasion of privacy by people with voyeuristic tendencies.  This bill proposes to penalize any person or persons found guilty of video or photo voyeurism with imprisonment for a period of at least eighteen months to a maximum of four years.

rows.author: C022
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING THE CRIME OF BETRAYAL OF DUTY IN THE CUSTODY OF PRISONERS, PROVIDING FOR ADDITIONAL RULES ON THE IMPRISONMENT, DETENTION, CONFINEMENT AND CUSTODY OF PRISONERS AND DETAINEES, SPECIFYING ADDITIONAL WORK AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF GOVERNMENT PERSONNEL CHARGED WITH THE CUSTODY OF SUCH PRISONERS AND STATING THE PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In many instances, a government official or employee commits the crime of betrayal of duty in the custody of prisoner because the penalty for such act is light and the inducement of a bribe is too great.  A guard who frees an inmate not only participates post litem to the commission of the crime of the offender but also turns traitor to the government and to the laws he has sworn to protect.  The bill seeks to define the crime of betrayal of duty in the custody of prisoners and provide stiffer penalties on the official or employee who has charge of the prisoner.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-08-04

rows.author: B016
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A NATIONAL BOOK DEVELOPMENT TRUST FUND TO SUPPORT FILIPINO AUTHORSHIP
rows.abstract: \"National Book Developemnt Trust Fund Act\".  Books are the most effective and economical tools for achieving intellectual growth; imparting information; and recording, preserving and disseminating the nation's cultural heritage.  However, most of the books available in our libraries and bookstores are not local publications.  This bill attempts to help both veteran and promising Filipino authors, specially those based outside of the National Capital Region, to produce or finish manuscripts for publication in the fields of science and technology, local history and in subject areas wherein local books are either few or non-existent.  It seeks to create a National Book Development Trust Fund through which grants can be offered to deserving authors.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2003-08-04

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ALLOCATION OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION SCHOOL BUILDING PROGRAM BUDGET, ENSURING BUDGET PRIORITY FOR THE CONSTRUCTION AND MAINTENANCE OF SCHOOL BUILDINGS AND CLASSROOMS, REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7880, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAIR AND EQUITABLE ACCESS TO EDUCATION ACT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The construction and maintenance of school buildings, classrooms and other facilities are essential to ensure a quality education.  However, most of our elementary and secondary public schools have inadequate classrooms.  The present budget allocation of the Department of Education (DepEd) including the School Building Program is not sufficient to cover the cost of much needed construction, repairs, rehabilitation and maintenance of school buildings and classrooms nationwide.  This bill proposes to allocate the budget of the School Building Program to each legislative district according to its classroom shortage as determined by the DepEd's Division Superintendent and District Supervisors.  It further proposes that the budget allocation for the construction of school buildings and classrooms be determined by the population of enrolled students in the elementary and secondary levels to be divided by forty (40).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2003-08-04

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE FULL IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL HEALTH INSURANCE PROGRAM' COMPULSORY COVERAGE FOR ALL FILIPINO RESIDENTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT 7875 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"NATIONAL HEALTH INSURANCE ACT OF 1995\", AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Philippine Health Insurance Program (Program) was created to provide health insurance coverage and to ensure affordable and accessible health care services to all citizens.  However, according to PhilHealth, the nationwide membership to the Program, including approved beneficiaries, is merely 6,334,320 members.  This number is dismally low considering that the Program projected the entire Philippine populace for its membership.  The bill provides for a mandatory coverage of all citizens of the Philippines under the Program and for its full and complete implementation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2003-08-04

rows.author: B013
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING INCENTIVES AND BENEFITS TO RURAL HEALTH DOCTORS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Rural Health Doctors Benefits and Incentives Act of 2001\".  The absence or shortage of doctors in the rural areas can be attributed to the lack of opportunities for rural doctors to provide for a comfortable and secure life for their families.  Majority of our competent and dedicated doctors are concentrated in urban areas or even abroad where the earnings are higher and the benefits more attractive.  This brain drain creates a vacuum in the rendering of health care in rural areas.  This bill seeks to boost the recruitment and retention of rural health doctors by granting them additional incentives and benefits.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2003-08-04

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A FEEDBACK MECHANISM IN THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES (AFP) AND THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE (PNP), CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE AFP/PNP WELFARE AND AFFAIRS OFFICE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: To enable our military and police personnel to perform their duties with utmost loyalty, the integrity of the military and police institutions must be upheld and the welfare of their personnel must be protected.  Their concerns and grievances must be addressed and resolved with dispatch and sincerity.  The recent rebellion by junior military officers reflects the prevailing sentiments and grievances within the military and police organizations.  The bill seeks to provide a feedback mechanism in the AFP and the PNP with the creation of the AFP/PNP Welfare and Affairs Office which would serve as the channel for the airing of legitimate grievances and concerns of both military and police personnel.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2003-08-04

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE INCLUSION OF BASIC ECONOMIC SUBJECTS AS PART OF THE CURRICULUM OF THE MILITARY AND POLICE COURSE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Coup d'etat, as an act of destabilization  against the duly constituted government and its authorities, gravely affects our political and economic stability.  In the interest of our nation's political and economic stability, This measure proposes to include basic economic subjects (Micro Economics 101 and Micro Economics 102)in the curriculum of military and police courses to provide their personnel with an understanding on the effects of destabilization acts and activities on the economy.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 2003-08-04

rows.author: C063
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF DERMATOLOGY IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Dermatology Act of 2003\".  Unqualified and untrained individuals pretending to be experts in the field of dermatology have sprouted in the country.  This has led to the proliferation of cases of malpractice leading to disfigurement, injury and even death.  To elevate the quality of dermatological care available to Filipinos, the bill seeks to regulate the practice of dermatology as a profession and to penalize the illegal practice of dermatology by incompetent individuals.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-08-04

rows.author: C097
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING SIKARAN AS THE NATIONAL MARTIAL ART OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to declare \"sikaran\" as the national martial art of the Philippines.  Sikaran-arnis is an ancient art of foot and stick fighting that originated in the town of Baras, Rizal.  It incorporates arnis in the predominantly foot-fighting technique making it distinct from the other forms of martial arts like taekwondo and karate.  Sikaran which is rapidly gaining popularity in the country, promotes the virtues of self-discipline and control as well as a healthy and simple lifestyle.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-08-04

rows.author: D060
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO INCLUDE VEHICLE TRAFFIC EDUCATION AS PART OF THE EDUCATIONAL CURRICULUM IN THE ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY LEVEL, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Traffic congestion is one of the major problems of the country.  Very often the safety of the riding public, particularly students, are compromised.  There is, therefore, a need to educate children on how to protect and safeguard themselves when on the road.  The bill seeks to authorize the Department of Education to include vehicular traffic education as part of the educational curriculum in the elementary and secondary levels.  The institutionalization of vehicular traffic education shall instill personal discipline and develop good values among the studentry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2003-08-04

rows.author: C060
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING HARBOR PILOTAGE SERVICES AND THE CONDUCT OF HARBOR PILOTS IN ALL PORTS IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Pilotage Service Act of 2003\".  Pilotage plays a vital and complementary role in the efficient operation of ports.  However, the Philippines still has to pass a pilotage act that would regulate this maritime activity in accordance with international principles of pilotage specially with respect to the pilot's liability in the event of damage to property or death and injury to persons caused by a vessek under pilotage.  This measure seeks to institutionalize prevailing practices in pilotage service, rationalize pilotage fees and other charges, and define the legal relationship between the harbor pilots and pilotage organizations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2003-08-04

rows.author: C017
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE TOTAL ELECTRIFICATION OF ALL OFF-GRID BARANGAYS IN THE COUNTRY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Off-Grid Barangay Electrification Act of 2003\".  The electrification of all barangays using new and renewable energy systems is envisioned to spur socio-economic growth in the countryside thus enhancing the quality of life in these areas.  While the electrification program has been in the government's thrust for over 30 years now, its completion remains unrealized due to financial and geographical constraints.  This bill seeks to appropriate one hundred million pesos (PhP100,000,000.00) to fund the electrification program of an estimated 1,978 off-grid barangays nationwide.  This represents 35.5% of the total unenergized barangays in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2003-08-04

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 223 OF ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: This measure proposes to impose a stiff penalty on jail guards and other persons who consent, connive or allow, by negligence, a prisoner in his custody or charge, to escape from the clutches of law.  Hopefully, this would deter those who are charged with the custody of prisoners, more specifically high profile detention prisoners, from allowing them to escape.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-08-04

rows.author: D011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SURVIVORSHIP BENEFITS TO SURVIVING SPOUSE OF RETIRED JUSTICE-PENSIONER WHO DIES WHILE RECEIVING HIS MONTHLY PENSION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED NIN HUNDRED TEN, AS AMENDED, ENTITLED \"AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE RETIREMENT OF JUSTICES OF THE SUPREME COURT AND OF THE COURT OF APPEALS, FOR THE ENFORCEMENT OF THE PROVISIONS HEREOF BY THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM, AND TO REPEAL COMMONWEALTH ACT NUMBERED FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY SIX\"
rows.abstract: The Government Service Insurance System and the Philippine Veterans Affairs Office grant survivorship benefits to qualified beneficiaries upon the death of an old-age pensioner or a member receiving monthly income benefit for permanent disability.  Identical benefits are also being given to the members of the constitutional commissions.  The bill proposes that survivorship benefits be extended also to the surviving spouse of a retired justice-pensioner who dies while receiving his monthly pension.  The proposed survivorship benefit shall be equivalent to 80% of the amount received by the retired justice-pensioner until the surviving spouse remarries or dies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-08-05

rows.author: D084
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND GUARANTEEING PUBLIC SECTOR UNIONISM IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Public Sector Unionism Act of 2002\".  Like their counterpart in the private sector, employees in the government service must be allowed to participate and involve themselves in the protection and promotion of their rights and welfare as employees.  This measure seeks to promote the welfare of government workers and guarantee their rights to self-organization, collective bargaining and negotiations and peaceful concerted activities including the right to strike.  The right to engage in peaceful concerted activities includes the right of government workers to peaceably assemble and petition the government for redress  of grievances.  The bill also seeks the creation of the Public Sector Labor Relations which shall have the original and exclusive jurisdiction to hear and decide, mandatorily, all cases arising from the implementation of the rights of government employees under this proposed act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-08-05

rows.author: B020
rows.title_full: AN ACT RE-IMPOSING THE GROSS RECEIPTS TAX ON SERVICES RENDERED BY BANKS, NON-BANK FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES, FINANCE COMPANIES AND OTHER FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES NOT PERFORMING QUASI-BANKING FUNCTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to re-impose gross receipts tax (GRT) on services rendered by banks, non-bank financial intermediaries, finance companies and other financial intermediaries not performing quasi-banking functions.  It introduces certain structural changes intended to harmonize the tax system with banking practices consistent with generally accepted accoounting principles and the requriements of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.  The re-imposition of the GRT is a more practical alternative to the value-added tax (VAT) on banks and other financial institutions.  The VAT on banks and other financial intermediaries is not only difficult to determine but may also have adverse effects on key segments of the financial services market.  The GRT system facilitates tax administration and compliance, rationalizes the sharing of the tax burden on financial transactions and is not expected to have a tremendous effect on the consumers of financial services.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2003-08-05

rows.author: D055
rows.title_full: AN ACT LIMITING THE EXPORTATION OF TROPICAL, ORNAMENTAL AND LIVE FOOD FISHES, PROVIDING FOR THE CONDUCT OF RESEARCH STUDIES FOR ALTERNATIVE FISHING METHODS OF CATCHING TROPICAL, ORNAMENTAL AND LIVE FOOD FISHES, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: The exportation of tropical and ornamental fishes accounted for .04% of the total fish exports from 1993 to 1995.  However, the market share of the industry can not compensate for the destructive effects of cyanide on the ecological balance of our marine ecosystem, particularly the corral reefs which serve as sanctuaries for ornamental and tropical fishes.  (At present, cyanide fishing is the most common fishing method employed by fishermen who catch tropical and ornamental fishes).  This measure imposes a mandatory ban on the exportation of such fishes for a minimum period of 10 years up to a maximum of 25 years to abate the use of cyanide on fishing unless an alternative fishing method for tropical and ornamental fishes is discovered.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2003-08-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A RATIONALIZED LAND ADMINISTRATION SYSTEM AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Land Administration System Act of 2003\".  The bill proposes to consolidate and streamline within  a single government agency the land administration powers and functions currently being dispersed by the Department of Justice's Land Registration Authority and Register of Deeds; the Department of Environment and Natural Resources' Land Management Bureau, Land Management Services in the regional, provincial and community offices, National Mapping and Resource Information Authority; and CARP Secretariat and its field offices.  Without the integration of these agencies, it will be difficult for the government to undertake major long-term investment of resources necessary in the implementation of over-all reforms.  The bill also seeks the creation of the Land Administration Authority which shall be the primary government agency responsible for land administration and public land management, specially the conduct of surveys, production of maps, classification of lands, disposition of alienable lands of the public domain and patrimonial lands, registration of titles, and resource information generation and management.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2003-08-05

rows.author: C022
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL LAND ADMINISTRATION AUTHORITY, RATIONALIZING THE ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT AGENCIES RELATED TO LAND ADMINISTRATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"National Land Administration ACt of 2003\".  The bill seeks to reform the existing land registration system under the Torrens system.  It aims to strengthen the Torrens system, streamline and simplify proceedings and issuance of Certificate of Title using automated machines.  It provides for the creation of the Land Administration Authority (LAA) which shall be the primary agency of the government that will prepare, integrate, coordinate, supervise and implement plans, programs, projects and activities relative to land administration functions.  The offices of the Land Management Bureau, Land Management Services, Land Registration Authority, National Mapping and Resource Information Authority, DENR CARP National Secretariat and the LRA-CARP shall be integrated under the LAA.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2003-12-15

rows.author: D028
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR GUIDELINES IN THE SELECTION AND APPOINTMENT OF A STATE UNIVERSITY/COLLEGE PRESIDENT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE \"HIGHER EDUCATION MODERNIZATION ACT OF 1997, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES\"
rows.abstract: This measure seeks to provide the guidelines in the selection of a state university/college president.  Said guideline will avert possible questions on the validity of the search committee's recommendation and assure a transparent process of selection.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2003-08-06

rows.author: D028
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS WHICH MAINTAIN ATHLETIC TEAMS TO ALLOW THEIR ATHLETES OR PLAYERS TO JOIN IN THE SELECTION POOL AND FORMATION OF PHILIPPINE NATIONAL TEAMS THAT WILL COMPETE IN ALL INTERNATIONAL SPORTS COMPETITIONS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: It is no secret that the Philippines lags behind in sports development compared to our Asian neighbors.  This is not due to a dearth of athletes but because of lack of cooperation and coordination among the government agencies concerned, educational institutional and the other sectors involved in the implementation of our sports program.  This bill seeks to require all educational institutions and athletic teams sponsored by commercial establishments to actively cooperate and assist the national government in the selection, training and formation of national teams that will compete in international sports competitions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2003-08-06

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROFESSIONALIZATION OF THE BUREAU OF FIRE PROTECTION (BFP) AND THE BUREAU OF JAIL MANAGEMENT AND PENOLOGY (BJMP), PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Bureau of Fire Protection and Bureau of Jail Management and Penology Professionalization Act of 2003\".  The uniformed personnel of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) and the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP), as members of the uniformed service of the government under  the Department of the Interior and Local Government, are required to put in the same amount of sacrifice and dedication as their counterparts in the Philippine National Police (PNP) and the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) to carry out their duties to the extent of risking their lives and limbs.  The bill seeks to professionalize and restructure the BFP and the BJMP by upgrading the level of qualifications of their uniformed personnel and standardizing their base pay, retirement and other benefits equivalent to those of the PNP and the AFP.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06557

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 97 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8550 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FISHERIES CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES OF 1998
rows.abstract: The Fisheries Code of the Philippines of 1998 is viewed by certain players in the aquaculture industry as unrealistic, oppressive and does not take into consideration new developments in aquaculture.  The bill seeks to define the term \"endangered species\" as referring to any of the rare marine life which is declining in number and is in danger of extinction and, for the purpose of this proposed act, are listed in the CITES (Convention on the International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora).  The proposed definition specifically excludes species which are replenished or grown by man with the the aid of research and technology and where actual propagation is in place assuring the preservation and increase in such marine life.

rows.author: D056
rows.title_full: AN ACT PUNISHING THE PILFERAGE OR THEFT OF ANY MATERIAL, PRODUCT, MERCHANDISE, ARTICLE, EQUIPMENT OR BY-PRODUCT MANUFACTURED, PRODUCED, OWNED, OR BELONGING TO INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY ENTERPRISES LOCATED IN SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Pilferage of Information Technology Materials in Special Economic Zones Act\".  The information technology (IT) industry has infused much needed capital into our economy.  It as also placed our country in the world map as one of the largest manufacturers of integrated circuit chips and other similar semiconductor products.  Unfortunately, because of their high value and compact size, theft and pilferage of this industry's products have risen.  These incidents of theft have adversely affected our competitiveness in the global arena.  This bill seeks to declare as unlawful for any person to take, pilfer or steal, any material, product, merchandise, article, equipment or by-product manufactured, produced, owned or belonging to IT enterprises located in special economic zones.  The passage of this measure would send a signal to the IT industry that the government is serious in protecting their economic rights.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-08-11

rows.author: C022
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RETIREMENT BENEFITS OF JUSTICES AND ALL JUDGES IN THE JUDICIARY, FURTHER AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION ONE OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED NINE HUNDRED AND TEN, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Under the GSIS Act of 1997, a member of the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) is eligible for retirement benefits when he/she has rendered at least fifteen (15) years of service and is at least sixty (60) years of age at the time of retirement.  To align the retirement benefits for justices and judges with that being offered under the GSIS Act of 1997, this bill seeks to reduce to fifteen (15) years of service the eligibility of a justice or judge who retires at the compulsory age of seventy (70) years to entitle him to receive the basic monthly pension for life starting at the end of the five-year guarantee period.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-08-11

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9164 TO EXTEND THE TERMS OF OFFICE OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND RESET THE DATE OF BARANGAY ELECTIONS
rows.abstract: The holding of election for barangay officials every three (3) years have proven to be very expensive for the government.  Furthermore, it gives politicians a chance to interfere in the barangay elections thereby creating an unstable peace and order situation in the barangays.  This bill proposes to extend the terms of office of barangay officials from three (3) years to four (4) years and, consequently, set the barangay election very four (4) years.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06691

rows.author: D104
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDEFINING THE CRIME OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT AND EXPANDING ITS COVERAGE, PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATORS THEREOF, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-EIGHT SEVENTY-SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS ANTI-SEXUAL HARASSMENT ACT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Reports indicate that sexual harassment cases remain common place.  They also reveal that government agencies, schools and private companies still have to comply with the requirements in RA 7877 (Anti-Sexual Harassment Act)for these institutions to formulate guidelines on sexual harassment and convene a Committee on Decorum to process complaints.  To strengthen the law and make it more effective, the bill proposes to redefine the crime of sexual harassment and expand its coverage to include those that occur in situations outside the work and education environments.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN since 2003-08-11

rows.author: D104
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF RAPE CRISIS CENTERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8505
rows.abstract: \"Women and Children Crisis Survivors Assistance and Protection Act of 2003\".  Violence against women and children is one of the pervasive forms of human rights abuse in our society.  Victims are often forced to endure situations of violence due to the lack of services that will support the decision to resist violence.  Shelter, employment, child care support, medical and legal assistance and psychological counseling are the common immediate needs of survivors of violence.  These can be provided by crisis center or shelter, community-based organizations, non-government organizations and government agencies.  The bill seeks to expand the coverage or rape crisis centers (established under RA 8505) to include victims of other forms of gender violence such as trafficked, prostituted and/or exploited women.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2003-08-11

rows.author: D104
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-05, transmitted to on 2004-02-09 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING BREASTFEEDING BY ESTABLISHING AND MAINTAINING LACTATION STATIONS IN WORKPLACES FOR WORKING MOTHERS PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ITS VIOLATION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Breastfeeding Promotion Act of 2003\".  Studies have shown that breastfeeding means better health for babies.  Aside from government and private hospitals, there are no facilities outside of the home where a mother can comfortably and privately breastfeed their babies.  This bill mandates the establishment of lactation stations in workplaces for nursing female employees.  The lactation station must be private, clean and well-ventilated and must have a lavatory for hand-washing, refrigeration for storage, and comfortable seats.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06661

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE MONTHLY INCOME BENEFITS FROM THE SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM FOR MEMBERS AND PENSIONERS WHO SUFFER FROM WORK-RELATED ILLNESS, OR HAVE DIED AS A RESULT OF WORK-RELATED CAUSES
rows.abstract: Through the years, the benefits from the Social Security System (SSS) have not increased substantially and have even depreciated because of worsening economic conditions and the corruption of government officials who have manipulated the SSS funds.  An increase in the benefits granted by the SSS would provide workers some relief from the effects of the economic crisis.  This bill proposes to grant a 25% across-the-board increase in the monthly income benefits for work-related illnesses, disability and death as a result of work-related causes with the proviso that no additional premium contributions shall be assessed upon the employees and the employers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2003-08-11

rows.author: D024
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 10(1) AND SECTION 11 OF REPUBLIC ACT 7156 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"MINI-HYDROELECTRIC POWER INCENTIVE ACT\"
rows.abstract: The MIni-Hydroelectric Power Incentive Act mandates the collection of a 2% special privilege tax (SPT) from mini-hydroelectric power developers.  The SPT shall be computed on the gross receipts from the sale of electric power and from transactions incident to the generation, transmission and sale of electric power.  It also grants the host local government units (LGUs) a 60% share on the SPT collections with the remaining 40% accruing to the national government.  The law also provides that the total SPT collections must first be remitted by the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) to the National Treasurer prior to release to the LGU concerned.  However, up to now, the LGUs still have to receive their share of the SPT collections.  To ensure receipt by the LGUs of their rightful share in the SPT collections, the bill proposes that 60% of the SPT collections be paid directly to the host LGU and that only the remaining 40% share of the national government be paid to the BIR.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2003-08-11

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PD 1638 BY DELETING THEREFROM SECTION 25(d), AND BY INSERTING IN ITS PLACE SECTION 9(d) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 340, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The pension of a retiree from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is computed based on the number of years he/she has actively served the AFP.  This is pursuant to Section 25 (d) of PD 1638 which provides that \"a year of active service shall mean 12 months\".  There are thousands of AFP personnel who retired under PD 1638 with a fraction of a year of service in addition to the full years of service.  These retirees are being shortchanged of benefits due them since a fraction of a year of service is not included in the computation of his monthly pension.  To correct this injustice, this bill proposes that any period of service totaling to six (6) months or more be considered as a complete year for purposes of computing the retirement benefits.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2003-08-11

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR ADDITIONAL DISQUALIFICATION FROM VOTER REGISTRATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 11 OF REPUBLIC ACT 8189, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE VOTER'S REGISTRATION ACT OF 1996
rows.abstract: Filipino soldiers swear to uphold, protect and defend the Constitution and to respect the supremacy of civilian authority over the military.  When soldiers betray their duty to the Constitution by committing the crime of rebellion, mutiny or sedition, insurrection or coup d'etat, they are deemed to have renounced their rights and privileges under the same Constitution they chose to abandon.  This bill proposes  that such betrayal of constitutional duty, specially the crime of mutiny, insurrection or coup d'etat and other related crimes, be penalized with perpetual disqualification from voter registration.  This disqualification from voter registration is tantamount to ineligibility to run for any public office.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2003-08-11

rows.title_full: AN ACT REPEALING SECTION 4 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 1 DATED FEBRUARY 28, 1986
rows.abstract: Section 4 (a) of Executive Order No. 1 grants the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) and its commissioners absolute immunity from all civil actions arising from any act or omission, whether in violation of the law or the rights of private individuals, as long as said act or omission is performed \"in the discharge of tasks contemplated by this order\".  It is an elementary principle however, that public officers are civilly liable for acts or omissions which violate the rights of private individuals.  The bill seeks to implement Section 1, Article XI of the Constitution in regard to the Commissioners, officers and employees of the PCGG.  It likewise seeks to repeal Section 4 of EO 1 through which Commissioners, officers and employees of the PCGG can claim \"a privileged status not claimed by other officials under the 1987 Constitution.

rows.author: D104
rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE THREE HUNDRED AND ONE (301) DAYS CRIMINAL PROHIBITION TO REMARRY AND ALLOWING THE REMARRIAGE OF A WIDOW OR A SEPARATED WOMAN FORTY (40) DAYS AFTER THE DEATH OF HER HUSBAND OR THE ANNULMENT OR DISSOLUTION OF HER PREVIOUS MARRIAGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 351 OF ACT NO. 3815 AS, AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"REVISED PENAL CODE\"
rows.abstract: The Revise Penal Code penalizes a woman who marries within 301 days from the date of the death of her husband and a woman who, her marriage having been annulled or dissolved, marries before the expiration of the period of 301 days after the date of the legal separation. This provision of the law is intended to prevent confusion with regard to filiation and paternity.  Advances in medical technology now allow the detection of pregnancy almost to the time of its inception.  This measure seeks to remove this discriminatory act against women by repealing the 301 days prohibition to remarry and reducing the same to 40 days in fealty to customs and traditions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-08-18

rows.author: D104
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 96, 124, 211 AND 225 OF THE NEW FAMILY CODE TO PROVIDE FOR JUDICIAL INTERVENTION IN CASES OF DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN HUSBAND AND WIFE OVER THE ADMINISTRATION AND ENJOYMENT OF COMMUNITY PROPERTY, THE ADMINISTRATION AND ENJOYMENT OF CONJUGAL PARTNERSHIP PROPERTY AND THE EXERCISE OF PARENTAL AUTHORITY AND LEGAL GUARDIANSHIP OVER THE PERSON AND PROPERTY OF UNEMANCIPATED COMMON CHILD
rows.abstract: The New Family Code, though largely adopting gender fair provisions, still retains certain provisions that give undue advantage to the husband over the wife.  This measure seeks to allow either party to seek judicial intervention in cases of disagreement between husband and wife over the administration and enjoyment of community and conjugal partnership property, and in the exercise of legal guardianship over the property of an unemancipated common child.  It also provides that in cases of disagreement in the exercise of parental authority, mother's decision shall prevail for children below 7 years old and for either party to go to court for proper remedy for children 7 years of age and above.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-08-18

rows.author: D100
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INSTITUTE COASTAL AND FORESHORE LAND REFORM
rows.abstract: Millions of Filipinos depend on small-scale fishing for their livelihood.  However, many of our small fishermen do not have direct and untrammeled access to the sea because most of the coastal lands are either lands of the public domain or private lands.  This bill aims to provide an opportunity for millions of small fishermen and farmer-fishermen to own small portions of the land along the coast by giving them the right to purchase the same under just and reasonable terms and conditions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2003-08-20

rows.author: D100
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ACQUISITION AND DISTRIBUTION OF MOISTURE METERS IN ALL COCONUT-PRODUCING BARANGAYS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: RA 1365 requires the use of moisture meters in all domestic purchases of copra for the purpose of ensuring good quality copra and better income for our coconut farmers.  It also prescribes a moisture content level for copra since high moisture content has been linked to high levels of aflatoxin which is known to cause cancer.  Unfortunately, the law has not been fully implemented due to lack of moisture meters.  The bill provides for the acquisition and distribution of moisture meters in all coconut-producing barangays in the country through the Philippine Coconut Authority.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2003-08-20

rows.author: D100
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE MANDATORY APPOINTMENT OF COOPERATIVE OFFICERS IN THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, GIVING THEM ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to foster the creation and growth of cooperatives as a vehicle for promoting self-reliance.  Under the Local Government Code of 1991, local executives are empowered, at their option, to appoint cooperative officers who shall take charge of the office for the development of cooperatives.  However, many local government units (LGUs) have not appointed their respective cooperative officers thus hampering the development of cooperatives in the country.  This measure seeks to address this problem by requiring the mandatory appointment of cooperative officers.  Its passage is expected to foster the formation of cooperatives as active partners of the LGUs in economic development specially in the rural areas.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2003-08-20

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND PENALIZING CRIMES AGAINST INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW AND OTHER SERIOUS INTERNATIONAL CRIMES, ADOPTING CORRESPONDING PRINCIPLES OF CRIMINAL RESPONSIBILITY, OPERATIONALIZING UNIVERSAL JURISDICTION, DESIGNATING SPECIAL COURTS AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Statute on Crimes Against International Humanitarian Law and Other Serious International Crimes\". It is the policy of the State to adopt the principles, rules and regulations of the Hague Convention and the Geneva Conventions on warfare and international humanitarian law to form part of the law of the land.  This measure seeks to consolidate these principles, rules and regulations in one comprehensive law in regard to the domestic penal aspect of serious international crimes.  It also seeks to define the international crime of genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and other crimes against international humanitarian law and to impose penalties for the commission of such crimes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-08-20

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE OFFICE OF THE GOVERNMENT NEGOTIATOR UNDER THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This measure seeks the creation of the Office of the Government Negotiator which shall act as the sole and principal negotiating office of the government in solving and monitoring crisis and conflict situations.  The Office shall represent the government in the settlement of conflicts involving armed or hostile individuals and groups.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2003-08-18
